Cc: Tom Keller <tkeller@aws-marketplace.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + regional split for coming year (PO attached)

Hi Mina,

Hope you had a good holiday. We're approaching our annual renewal window for the private offer covering Aria Health. We need to: 
- split the committed capacity 60/40 across us-west-2 and us-east-1 for compliance and DR testing,
- add a 6-month ramp clause allowing a 20% burst beyond committed capacity during Q2, and
- preserve monthly usage reporting with a dedicated billing contact.

Attached is our PO draft (Aria_PO_1234.pdf). Can Redwood accept a multi-region acceptance window (we want initial acceptance in us-west-2, with a subsequent 30-day acceptance for us-east-1) or do we need two separate private offers? Also, any internal notes on handling credits if us-east-1 ramps slower than expected?

Tom — CCing you for AWS marketplace implications (we may hit private offer constraints).

Next steps: can your team confirm whether a single private offer can be configured to cover both regions with staggered acceptance? If not, advise on the cleanest workaround so procurement can issue the PO.

Thanks,
Aria Sharma
Procurement Manager
Aria Health

Attachment: Aria_PO_1234.pdf (application/pdf, 78KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + regional split for coming year (PO attached)

Hi Aria — thanks for the PO and clear asks. Short answers up front: 
1) A single AWS private offer can support multi-region SKUs, but the acceptance window and billing topology are typically tied to the marketplace listing and may require an acceptance workaround (we've done staged acceptance via an initial acceptance + a follow-up amendment).
2) Credits/True-ups: we can map unused committed capacity in the second region to credits or a carry-forward bucket for a single 12‑month term, but that requires explicit language in the PO and in the private-offer attachment.

I'll loop in Marissa (contracts & marketplace coordination) and Ben (billing) to propose exact wording and the operational playbook. Proposed immediate next steps:
- Redwood to supply a short template amendment that adds a 30-day secondary acceptance window and a burst clause.
- Aria to confirm billing contact and whether invoice monthly or quarterly.
- If AWS requires separate private-offer records, we'll coordinate issuance and DocuSign sequencing so your procurement team sees a single logical package.

I'll attach the AWS private-offer template and a sample amendment in a follow-up.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Renewals — Redwood Inference

Attachment references: aws-private-offer-template.pdf (stub)

Mina / Ben — quick internal working thread before I reply to Aria and loop AWS. Notes below: 

On the private-offer mechanics:
- AWS private offers accept one primary acceptance event. To implement a staggered acceptance we issue the primary acceptance for us-west-2 and then a targeted amendment for us-east-1. That keeps marketplace accounting aligned.
- For the ramp/burst: we can add a 20% temporary burst with explicit cap and a single reconciliation at the end of Q2. Legal prefers a defined measurement window (e.g., daily max vs monthly aggregate).

Contract language (draft lines):
- "Buyer may accept initial SKU(s) for us-west-2 upon signature; Buyer shall have 30 calendar days following primary acceptance to accept additional SKU(s) scoped to us-east-1 via Seller-issued amendment. Unaccepted SKU capacity that remains unused after 60 days may be converted to account credit at a rate of X per token."

Billing + invoicing:
- Ben: recommend monthly invoices to match Aria's finance cadence. Need billing contact (Aria to confirm).

Can we aim to send the draft amendment + AWS private-offer flow to Aria by EOD Wednesday? If so, I'll include a short ops checklist for acceptance sequencing (who signs first, DocuSign order, marketplace acceptance by Redwood ops, and final invoice cut).

-Marissa
Senior Marketplace Programs Manager
